Tempe's Gen Digital Eyes GoDaddy in $11.8B Deal, Markets React Fast
Source: Tony Webster / Wikimedia Commons
Gen Digital, the Tempe-based cybersecurity company behind Norton, Avast and LifeLock, has made a preliminary approach to acquire fellow Tempe company GoDaddy in a potential deal valued at $11.8 billion. The approach, first reported in recent weeks, would combine two of the Valley's largest public software companies into a single business spanning website hosting, domain registration, payments and consumer cybersecurity.
According to the Phoenix Business Journal, Gen Digital made its first acquisition offer for GoDaddy in recent weeks, though discussions between the two companies remain in the early stages with no guaranteed deal. The $11.8 billion figure comes from a separate report by bizjournals.com, even as other accounts of the talks note that financial terms and deal structure have not been disclosed. The Financial Times reported that Gen Digital made a preliminary offer for GoDaddy in recent weeks, according to Yahoo Finance, which added that no offer structure, signed agreement, board recommendation or timeline had been disclosed.
GoDaddy manages 81 million website domains and provides domain registration, website hosting, website-building tools and payments services primarily to small businesses and individual customers, per the same Yahoo Finance report. A combination would bring those businesses together with Gen Digital's Norton, Avast and LifeLock cybersecurity portfolio, and would give Gen Digital access to GoDaddy's base of 20 million small business customers, the Phoenix Business Journal reports.
Markets Swing Hard in Opposite Directions
Wall Street's reaction was immediate and lopsided. GoDaddy shares spiked as much as 11% after news of the approach broke, while Gen Digital's stock slid nearly 8% at the time of publication, the same Yahoo Finance account notes. Elsewhere, shares of Gen Digital fell 12.05% to $23.07 while GoDaddy rose 4.64% to $100.85 following the takeover report, per the earlier Yahoo Finance article covering the reaction.
Both companies have so far declined to comment on the reported approach. Gen Digital CEO Vincent Pilette told analysts he could not comment on the rumors when asked directly, according to Investing.com. Pilette did lay out the criteria Gen Digital uses to weigh any acquisition — strategic fit, price, efficiency creation, accretion, and value relative to share buybacks — while stressing the importance of maintaining a strong balance sheet, the outlet reported.
This wouldn't be Gen Digital's first major purchase. The company, formed through the merger of NortonLifeLock and Avast according to Gurufocus, acquired MoneyLion in a $1 billion deal in 2025. Pilette pointed to Avast and MoneyLion as successful past acquisitions, per the same Investing.com report, adding that the MoneyLion deal is on track to deliver more than a 30% return on invested capital in its second year.
Not everyone expects history to repeat itself with GoDaddy, however. RBC analyst Matthew Hedberg said Gen Digital is unlikely to pursue the previously rumored acquisition, according to Gurufocus, which reported that Gen Digital appeared to be prioritizing share repurchases and organic growth instead of a large-scale acquisition. Gen Digital has also raised its fiscal 2027 revenue growth guidance to 9%-11%, Investing.com noted, suggesting the company sees plenty of room to grow on its own.
Whatever happens with Gen Digital's approach, GoDaddy has been posting strong numbers independently. Heading into the end of September on a bearish note, shares of Corning (GLW +2.35%) are tumbling lower. With an analyst taking a neutral stance on the tech stock, investors are sensing that today's a good time to click the sell button.
As of 3:00 p.m. ET, shares of Corning are down 3.1%.
Image source: Getty Images.
Networking stocks are poised to prosper due to AI spending
Initiating coverage with a sector perform rating, Bernstein analyst Daniel Zhu set a $140 price target on Corning stock. Based on Corning's closing price of $158.71 yesterday, Zhu's price target implies a 13.4% downside.
$141BMarket cap calculated using publicly traded shares outstanding only. Does not include unlisted, private, or dual-class non-traded shares. Implied market cap may vary.
According to Thefly.com, Zhu broadly believes that the significant investments companies are making in developing artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure will benefit companies specializing in networking and optical solutions, with demand outpacing supply.
The other catalyst for the tech stock's fall today may simply be that investors are taking profits after Corning stock soared yesterday following news that the company had secured a supply agreement with AT&T worth more than $3 billion.
Is Corning stock a buy on the analyst's bearish outlook?
While Zhu's $140 price target may be disappointing to current shareholders -- and potentially dissuade potential investors from starting a position -- it's critical to remember that this is merely one analyst's opinion. A leader in manufacturing optical fiber and specialized glass, Corning is at the forefront of providing materials used in various types of today's tech. Potential investors should therefore take the analyst's price target with a grain of salt and weigh the company's financial health more heavily -- a much better indicator of the stock's allure.

This wouldn't be Gen Digital's first major purchase. The company, formed through the merger of NortonLifeLock and Avast according to Gurufocus, acquired MoneyLion in a $1 billion deal in 2025. Not everyone expects history to repeat itself with GoDaddy, however. RBC analyst Matthew Hedberg said Gen Digital is unlikely to pursue the previously rumored acquisition, according to Gurufocus, which reported that Gen Digital appeared to be prioritizing share repurchases and organic growth instead of a large-scale acquisition. Gen Digital has also raised its fiscal 2027 revenue growth guidance to 9%-11%, Investing.com noted, suggesting the company sees plenty of room to grow on its own.
Whatever happens with Gen Digital's approach, GoDaddy has been posting strong numbers independently. Can Corning's AT&T Deal Boost Its Optical Communications Growth?
Thu, October 1, 2026 at 6:40 AM PDT 2 min read
Corning Incorporated GLW has secured a multi-year agreement worth more than $3 billion with AT&T Inc. T to expand high-speed broadband infrastructure in the United States. The deal strengthens Corning's position in optical communications as rising data consumption and artificial intelligence (AI) adoption drive greater demand for advanced connectivity.
Under the agreement, Corning will provide the fiber and cable required for AT&T's network expansion, supporting connectivity for residential customers, businesses and communities. Its fiber and connectivity solutions are expected to accelerate network deployment, improve installation efficiency and support the domestic connectivity supply chain.
Corning is also expanding its fiber and cable production in the United States, including a North Carolina facility that has created hundreds of jobs. These investments will increase the company's manufacturing capacity and strengthen its ability to supply fiber solutions for next-generation network infrastructure.
Corning has also partnered with Verizon Communications Inc. VZ to provide fiber and connectivity solutions for broadband expansion and AI-related infrastructure. As telecom companies continue to invest in higher-capacity networks, Corning is likely to benefit from sustained demand for optical fiber and related solutions, supporting its growth opportunities in the communications market.
How Are Competitors Focusing on Fiber?
Corning faces competition from Amphenol Corporation APH and Lumen Technologies, Inc. LUMN. Amphenol is strengthening its fiber-optic capabilities to meet growing demand from data centers and AI applications. The company is seeing strong demand for fiber-based connectivity as customers upgrade networks to support higher data speeds and capacity. Amphenol's expanding portfolio of fiber-optic and interconnect products helps meet the growing need for reliable, high-speed data transmission.
Lumen is adding new fiber routes and network capacity as AI workloads drive greater data traffic across the United States. Its NorthLine project will connect Seattle and Minneapolis through a low-latency route designed to support high-capacity data movement between data centers and cloud networks. Lumen is expanding its network infrastructure to meet the growing connectivity needs of businesses, data centers and AI applications.
Corning's Price Performance, Valuation & Estimates
Shares of Corning have rallied 85.0% over the past year compared with the industry's growth of 130.4%.
From a valuation standpoint, the company's shares currently trade at 38.14 forward 12-month earnings, higher than the industry tally of 35.07.
Corning's earnings estimates for 2026 have increased 0.9% to $3.28 per share, while the same for 2027 have risen 0.7% to $4.28 over the past 60 days.

Can Corning's AT&T Deal Boost Its Optical Communications Growth?
Thu, October 1, 2026 at 6:40 AM PDT 2 min read
Corning Incorporated GLW has secured a multi-year agreement worth more than $3 billion with AT&T Inc. T to expand high-speed broadband infrastructure in the United States. The deal strengthens Corning's position in optical communications as rising data consumption and artificial intelligence (AI) adoption drive greater demand for advanced connectivity.
Under the agreement, Corning will provide the fiber and cable required for AT&T's network expansion, supporting connectivity for residential customers, businesses and communities. Its fiber and connectivity solutions are expected to accelerate network deployment, improve installation efficiency and support the domestic connectivity supply chain.
Corning is also expanding its fiber and cable production in the United States, including a North Carolina facility that has created hundreds of jobs. These investments will increase the company's manufacturing capacity and strengthen its ability to supply fiber solutions for next-generation network infrastructure.
Corning has also partnered with Verizon Communications Inc. VZ to provide fiber and connectivity solutions for broadband expansion and AI-related infrastructure. As telecom companies continue to invest in higher-capacity networks, Corning is likely to benefit from sustained demand for optical fiber and related solutions, supporting its growth opportunities in the communications market.
How Are Competitors Focusing on Fiber?
Corning faces competition from Amphenol Corporation APH and Lumen Technologies, Inc. LUMN. Amphenol is strengthening its fiber-optic capabilities to meet growing demand from data centers and AI applications. The company is seeing strong demand for fiber-based connectivity as customers upgrade networks to support higher data speeds and capacity. Amphenol's expanding portfolio of fiber-optic and interconnect products helps meet the growing need for reliable, high-speed data transmission.
Lumen is adding new fiber routes and network capacity as AI workloads drive greater data traffic across the United States. Its NorthLine project will connect Seattle and Minneapolis through a low-latency route designed to support high-capacity data movement between data centers and cloud networks. Lumen is expanding its network infrastructure to meet the growing connectivity needs of businesses, data centers and AI applications.
Corning's Price Performance, Valuation & Estimates
Shares of Corning have rallied 85.0% over the past year compared with the industry's growth of 130.4%.
From a valuation standpoint, the company's shares currently trade at 38.14 forward 12-month earnings, higher than the industry tally of 35.07.
Corning's earnings estimates for 2026 have increased 0.9% to $3.28 per share, while the same for 2027 have risen 0.7% to $4.28 over the past 60 days.
Corning currently has a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

Heading into the end of September on a bearish note, shares of Corning (GLW +2.35%) are tumbling lower. With an analyst taking a neutral stance on the tech stock, investors are sensing that today's a good time to click the sell button.
As of 3:00 p.m. ET, shares of Corning are down 3.1%.

Networking stocks are poised to prosper due to AI spending
Initiating coverage with a sector perform rating, Bernstein analyst Daniel Zhu set a $140 price target on Corning stock. Based on Corning's closing price of $158.71 yesterday, Zhu's price target implies a 13.4% downside.

According to Thefly.com, Zhu broadly believes that the significant investments companies are making in developing artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure will benefit companies specializing in networking and optical solutions, with demand outpacing supply.
The other catalyst for the tech stock's fall today may simply be that investors are taking profits after Corning stock soared yesterday following news that the company had secured a supply agreement with AT&T worth more than $3 billion.
Is Corning stock a buy on the analyst's bearish outlook?
While Zhu's $140 price target may be disappointing to current shareholders -- and potentially dissuade potential investors from starting a position -- it's critical to remember that this is merely one analyst's opinion. A leader in manufacturing optical fiber and specialized glass, Corning is at the forefront of providing materials used in various types of today's tech. Potential investors should therefore take the analyst's price target with a grain of salt and weigh the company's financial health more heavily -- a much better indicator of the stock's allure.

Heading into the end of September on a bearish note, shares of Corning (GLW +2.35%) are tumbling lower. With an analyst taking a neutral stance on the tech stock, investors are sensing that today's a good time to click the sell button.
As of 3:00 p.m. ET, shares of Corning are down 3.1%.
Image source: Getty Images.
Networking stocks are poised to prosper due to AI spending
Initiating coverage with a sector perform rating, Bernstein analyst Daniel Zhu set a $140 price target on Corning stock. Based on Corning's closing price of $158.71 yesterday, Zhu's price target implies a 13.4% downside.
$141BMarket cap calculated using publicly traded shares outstanding only. Does not include unlisted, private, or dual-class non-traded shares. Implied market cap may vary.
According to Thefly.com, Zhu broadly believes that the significant investments companies are making in developing artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure will benefit companies specializing in networking and optical solutions, with demand outpacing supply.
The other catalyst for the tech stock's fall today may simply be that investors are taking profits after Corning stock soared yesterday following news that the company had secured a supply agreement with AT&T worth more than $3 billion.
Is Corning stock a buy on the analyst's bearish outlook?
While Zhu's $140 price target may be disappointing to current shareholders -- and potentially dissuade potential investors from starting a position -- it's critical to remember that this is merely one analyst's opinion. A leader in manufacturing optical fiber and specialized glass, Corning is at the forefront of providing materials used in various types of today's tech. Potential investors should therefore take the analyst's price target with a grain of salt and weigh the company's financial health more heavily -- a much better indicator of the stock's allure.
